hero.title: The Four Noble Truths (Chatvari Arya Satyani)
hero.description: The philosophical foundation of Buddhism explaining the nature of suffering and the path to liberation (Nirvana).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Concepts

  • Dukkha: Life is inherently painful.
  • Samudaya: Tanha (Desire) is the cause.
  • Nirodha: Suffering can be eliminated.
  • Magga: The Eightfold Path is the way.

Key Philosophers

  • Gautama Buddha: Proponent.
  • Sariputta: Chief Disciple.
  • Ashoka: Patron and propagator.
  • Mindmap Overview:
    • Nature of Existence: Impermanence (Anicca) and Soul-less (Anatta).
    • Psychological focus: Controlling mental states to end the cycle of rebirth (Samsara).

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The emergence of the Four Noble Truths during the 6th century BCE as part of the Shramana movement.

cards.details: Gautama Buddha delivers the Dhammachakkappavattana Sutta at Sarnath, establishing the Four Noble Truths.
Ashoka the Great institutionalizes these principles across his edicts after the Kalinga War.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks
mnemonics.description: Recall the truths using the medical diagnosis framework.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming the 4 Noble Truths imply nihilism; Buddhism is actually a path of balance (Middle Path).
Thinking the 4 Noble Truths are exclusive to Mahayana; they are the bedrock of Theravada.
